messages:
kevin: Heads-up: partner-APAC opened a ticket — massive duplicate usage records during last maintenance window. They see ~4k duplicate units across multiple customers. Can we triage quickly?

sophia: ouch. do we know which integration version they're on? duplicates usually from missing idempotency + replay.

kevin: they're on v1.2. Partner payloads include both `id` and `provider_id`. Their SDK rotates `id` per attempt; provider_id is stable. Seems our consumer was deduping on `id` for that legacy mapping.

anya: tagging ingest owners  @jake any chance our windowing for usage aggregation mis-merged events across timezone boundaries? partner said their system submitted at the top of each minute.

jake: checking logs. Our webhook consumer used `id` as dedupe key for v1 integrations. Newer spec expects `provider_id`. Additionally, our TTL for in-flight dedupe keys is 5 minutes, partner retried after 10 minutes when edge returned 502, so duplicates slipped through.

jake: also noticed their timestamps are sometimes in local TZ without offset. That caused off-by-hour grouping into a different usage window, inflating counts in some invoice periods.

finance-ops: approximate billing impact? we need to know if invoices already went out. If so, credits + CS notifications required.

kevin: partner says 12 invoices touched. Rough estimate: ~4k units -> ~$1.1k gross charge. We'll need a formal reconcile and credit CSV.

anya: immediate mitigation: 1) implement short-term per-key soft throttle for that partner to 2 TPS; 2) add temporary acceptance rule that treats `provider_id` as canonical if present; 3) request partner pause replay until we sign off.

jake: I can push a hotfix to prefer `provider_id` when present and extend dedupe TTL to 24h for their API key. Deploy to staging in 30m. Will also add a payload-hash check so replayed payloads with identical body are merged even if id differs.

ingest-bot: [alert] 1935006789 - detected 128 anomalous duplicate events from partner-APAC between 1935003600-1935005400. duplicate_rate=0.24%

sophia: long-term: update onboarding doc and contract: require `X-Redwood-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256), `X-Redwood-Idempotency` header, and stable `provider_id` in body. Provide sample curl and replay checklist.

kevin: draft to partner: "We traced duplicates to legacy id mapping + retries after edge 502. We'll run a deterministic reconciliation, issue credits for any billed duplicates, and publish an updated webhook contract requiring HMAC + idempotency header and canonical provider_id. Please pause any replays until we confirm the reconcile."

cs-team: pls include a customer-facing script for how credits will appear and timeline. We should proactively message affected accounts with estimated amounts and next steps.

finance-ops: once reconcile CSV is ready, send to billing@ with invoice refs. We'll batch credits for the next billing cycle and mark invoices as adjusted. Need a signed approval from partner for the replay file before we ingest any retro events.

kevin: agreed. Plan of record: 1) stop partner replay; 2) patch consumer (prefer provider_id + payload-hash dedupe) -> staging -> canary -> prod; 3) run SQL to detect duplicates and generate credit CSV; 4) partner signs replay file with HMAC, we verify and then accept ordered replays; 5) issue credits and notify customers. ETA 24-36h.

jake: opened PR #4527 for mapping change and payload-hash. Will coordinate SRE for throttle and canary.

kevin: I'll send the contract amendment + replay checklist. Copying in finance and CS for follow-up. :thumbsup:
